text:
Oh, whiteness. Who placed in our lives,

lives of frantic abyssal beasts,

this brightness of sidereal lights,

these snows, inflamed with dream?


Oh sweet little pursued beasts.

Oh smooth touch. Oh zenithal signs.

Oh musics. Oh flames. Oh crystals.

Oh tall sails, risen from the sea.


Ah, timid gleams, pure dawn,

who brought you to this hard man's chest,

to this black uproar of hatred and forgetting?


Sweet specters, clouds, vain flowers...

Oh tender shadows, vaguely human,

sad women, made of air or of moan!

translation.title: Women
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the historical diction and the poem's movement from celestial whiteness to ghostly human sorrow.
